tagline: Buran's atmospheric analog — equivalent of NASA's Enterprise. Four jet engines, 24 atmospheric tests 1985-88, never to orbit
description: Officially BTS-002, nicknamed OK-GLI. Full-scale atmospheric test article for the Buran orbital programme — same outer mold-line as the flight vehicle Buran 1.01 but fitted with four AL-31 turbojet engines so it could take off under its own power from a conventional runway. 24 atmospheric flights between 1985-11-10 and 1988-04-15 at the Zhukovsky Flight Research Institute airfield validated Buran's automated landing system + flight-control software for the 1988-11-15 orbital flight. After the Buran programme cancellation OK-GLI sat at LII for years; sold to an Australian museum in 1999, then Bahrain, finally to the Technik Museum Speyer / Sinsheim in Germany where it is on display today — Buran's equivalent of NASA's Enterprise.
best_known_for: Buran's atmospheric analog; 24 jet-powered flights 1985-88 at Zhukovsky; never to orbit
